- The rule-framed composer means turn-complete. I treat composerTop ≤ endRow (a full-width-rule pair, per chrome.ts) as the witness that the agent finished its turn,
  so everything above it is sealable. The working spinner is a marker line, not rule-framed, so it correctly does not seal — keeping a still-streaming report
  provisional.

- Scrollback is immutable. No code clears scrollback (ESC[3J) or relies on rewriting scrolled-off lines; reflow-on-resize preserves logical content. Alt-screen is
  already excluded.

- One quiet scan may be all we get, so the provisional bottom unit is emitted promptly (visible to the user) even before it's sealed — sealing only governs re-scan,
  not visibility.

- Re-scanning the provisional tail is bounded. Once content scrolls, baseY-1 seals scrollback so the scan window stays ~viewport-sized; only the degenerate "everything
  fits on screen, no composer" case re-scans from row 0, and that buffer is tiny.

- Truncation when there's no seal frontier is edge-triggered off a captured unit's start-marker trimming (fires once, then forgotten), preserving the existing
  truncated signal without a separate marker.
